A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Graph Unitary Message Passing, with clearly corresponding algorithms, experiments, and mathematical foundations. The complete main texts and appendices are readable and support comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original GUMP results on TU and LRGB datasets, alongside Jacobian, network-depth, and component-ablation experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original benchmark and synthetic-task results, plus appendix experiments on molecular and node classification, projection diagnostics, and runtime.

M1.justification: Algorithm 2 changes from exact blockwise polar projection in v1 to normalized, finite-step Newton–Schulz projection in v2. This changes the computed propagation operator to an approximation with an iteration-dependent accuracy tradeoff. The underlying line-graph transformation, attention weights, and scatter/concatenation architecture remain recognizable.

E1.justification: v2 adds CrossedRing, Ring, and CliquePath synthetic tasks, ogbg-molhiv molecular classification, and Cora/Citeseer node classification. It removes IMDB-Binary and PCQM-contact throughout the paper and appendices, eliminating the previously evaluated link-prediction task. Five TU datasets and the two peptide tasks remain.

E2.justification: The retained TU comparison gains ELDANADD, ADGN, GRAND, GPS, Ortho-GConv, GRIT, and Kiani et al. The LRGB comparison adds numerous methods, including Exphormer, Graph ViT, G-MLPMixer, Drew-GCN, and k-GCN-SSM. Appendix Figure 6 also adds ADGN and Drew to the Jacobian comparison. These are reported comparisons, not merely new citations.

E3.justification: New protocols include synthetic distances 4–28 with depth tied to distance, official scaffold-split ROC-AUC evaluation on ogbg-molhiv, block diagnostics at tolerance 10^-7 with five versus ten projection iterations, and runtime comparisons with matched propagated-node budgets. The main Jacobian sweep extends to 200 layers. LRGB now references the Tönshoff evaluation protocol and flags Kiani et al.'s different setup; common TU split proportions and listed hyperparameters are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix D.1 adds substantial tests of block rank, conditioning, and finite-step projection accuracy using random continuous representations. v2 also adds synthetic distance stress tests, extends depth/Jacobian analyses, compares ADGN and Drew's Jacobian behavior, and measures computational overhead under two batching controls. The original component ablations and NCI1 accuracy-versus-depth analysis largely remain.

E5.justification: v2 explicitly reports averaging three random seeds for the new synthetic experiments. Both versions retain 100 random TU train/validation splits and 95% confidence intervals. The PDFs do not establish increased repetitions or a changed uncertainty-estimation procedure for the retained benchmark experiments.

E6.justification: v2 adds synthetic, molecular, node-classification, projection, and runtime results. Reported peptide AP changes from 0.6843 to 0.7088 and MAE from 0.2564 to 0.2438; these are revised reports with method/protocol differences, not established same-setting gains. TU results are internally unreconciled: v2 Table 1 gives GIN-GUMP ENZYMES accuracy 53.11±5.80, while v1 Table 2 and v2 Appendix Table 7 give 48.43±1.24.

T1.justification: v1's expected-Jacobian O(1) versus O(c^L) theorems are replaced by a newly defined source-averaged row-energy quantity, exact unitary conservation at 1/N, and decay bounds for normalized propagation's non-stationary component. v2 explicitly separates gate and weight assumptions, adds admissible-transition support preservation, repairs the existence argument for disconnected graphs, and substantially revises the corresponding proofs.

C1.justification: v1 presents GUMP as achieving an optimal oversquashing Jacobian measure while preserving structural bias. v2 refocuses the contribution on stability of the aggregate graph-propagation factor under explicit assumptions and preservation of admissible edge-to-edge transitions. Its abstract also uses competitive-or-superior performance claims against stronger comparisons. These substantially narrow and redefine the central claims.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly states that row-energy conservation guarantees neither individual source-target influence nor a depth-invariant full Jacobian. It qualifies the Jacobian plots as directionally consistent with the theory rather than direct validation of its quantity. Limitations now analyze degree-sensitive expansion costs and the exact-theory/finite-iteration gap, supported by numerical diagnostics and runtime evidence, substantially extending v1's brief computational caveats.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability URL and specifies the previously abstract Scatter operation as an incoming-edge mean, with zero output for isolated nodes. It supplies synthetic-task hyperparameters, numerical-diagnostic initialization and tolerance, CPU information, and training-time/batching details. Shared benchmark hyperparameter rows largely persist. The iteration budget used for the main accuracy results remains unspecified.

R1.justification: Related work expands from oversquashing and unitary networks to oversmoothing, line-graph and edge-centric methods, newer recurrent architectures, and unitary optimization. Appendix A adds substantial positioning against CensNet, LGLP, LGCL, and related approaches. v2 also explicitly distinguishes its construction from Kiani et al.'s 2024 unitary graph convolutions and discusses their different computational bottlenecks.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around training stability. Main-text related work moves to Appendix A, Section 2 becomes unitarity/stability preliminaries, and the conclusion becomes an expanded discussion of limitations. Method explanations and theoretical exposition are substantially reorganized; authorship and publication headers also change.

P2.justification: v2 switches the main paper from two-column to single-column layout, redesigns the overview, and adds an introductory results figure. The retained TU comparison moves into Appendix Table 7 while a broader main comparison is introduced. Synthetic plots and diagnostic, molecular, node-classification, and runtime tables are added; model-analysis axes, legends, and table highlighting are revised.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the central reasoning by replacing v1's overly broad Jacobian conclusions with explicit row-energy conservation and a stationary/non-stationary spectral analysis. Stronger comparisons, numerical diagnostics, reproducibility details, and measured computational limitations make the evidence more informative. Unexplained TU table discrepancies, removal of two benchmarks, and the remaining exact-theory/approximate-implementation gap are material drawbacks, but the corrected theoretical scope and expanded validation provide a clear substantial net improvement.
